claims.text: Multi-principal-element synergy in Cr-containing high-entropy alloys reduces cation mobility at high temperature.
Reduced cation mobility drives early nucleation of a protective oxide layer.
The resulting chromia/spinel-type layer is dense and persists during high-temperature exposure.
The protective layer suppresses further outward metal diffusion.
The protective layer reduces oxide-scale spallation.
Cr-containing high-entropy alloys have better oxidation resistance than simpler Cr-bearing alloys because of this synergy-based mechanism.
High-temperature in situ XRD can monitor oxide-phase formation and transformation in CrMnFeCoNi in real time up to 1100 °C.
Atom probe tomography can continuously monitor cation profiles in real time during the high-temperature oxidation exposure.
The stable scale on CrMnFeCoNi is predominantly Cr2O3 or a spinel such as MnCr2O4.
Collective diffusion constraints in the high-entropy matrix cause formation of the stable multi-cation scale.
Sluggish outward migration of alloy constituents promotes formation of a continuous and adherent oxide scale.
A continuous compact protective scale produces low oxide-growth kinetics.
The protective scale undergoes minimal volatilization at 900–1100 °C.
Under identical oxidation conditions, the high-entropy alloy will form a thinner scale than the stainless-steel baseline.
Under identical oxidation conditions, the high-entropy alloy will show lower mass gain than the stainless-steel baseline.
The high-entropy alloy will retain more stable oxide phases at the metal/oxide interface than the stainless-steel baseline.
Cr-bearing 304 or 310 stainless steel forms chromia scales.
The stainless-steel baseline will oxidize faster than CrMnFeCoNi under identical conditions.
At least approximately 15 at.% Cr is required for the proposed protective behavior.
At temperatures above approximately 1100 °C, competing nonprotective oxides may dominate.

contradictions.description: The intervention treats air as an example of the selected oxygen partial pressure, whereas the conditions specify 1 atm O2; air has a substantially lower oxygen partial pressure and is not equivalent to pure oxygen at 1 atm.
